newsitem.title: USA: Gull to acquire Fresenius Diagnostics.
newsitem.headline: Gull to acquire Fresenius Diagnostics.

text.p: Gull Laboratories Inc, said Wednesday it has signed an agreement to acquire the diagnostics business of Fresenius AG's intensive care and diagnostics division.

Under the proposed deal, Gull said it will pay Fresenius 1.32 million additional shares of its common stock. As a result, Fresenius' stake in Gull, which the German company operates as a consolidated subsidiary since 1994, will increase to 62 percent, from 55 percent, Gull said.

The business to be acquired offers blood-typing test sera and reagents for human leukocyte antigen tissue typing, test kits to diagnose infectious and autoimmunue diseases and automated systems. It sells its products in Germany and elsewhere in Europe and had sales of $8.3 million in 1996.
The acquisition must be approved by the non-Fresenius shareholders of Gull and the transaction is expected to be completed by the middle of 1997, Gull said.
Gull said it expects the combination to strengthen its position in the European diagnostics market through better customer orientation and more efficient marketing and sales.

In 1996 Gull posted sales of $17.9 million, of which 37 percent came from business in Europe, principally in Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, and 63 percent from the United States and the rest of the world. Profits after taxes amounted to $241,000.

Gull makes and markets diagnostic test kits for cardiovascular disease, infectious diseases and autoimmune disorders. It also offers a line of instrumentation for laboratory automation of immunoassay test kits.
Fresenius is an international company which develops, manufactures and distributes pharmaceutical and medical systems products.
